title: Obedience to the Word
definition: Obedience to the Word is the faithful response of trusting, submitting to, and practicing what God commands and teaches in Scripture.
summary: God's Word is not given merely to be heard, admired, debated, or memorized. It is given to lead His people into faith, repentance, worship, holiness, love, endurance, and mission.
christFocus: Jesus perfectly obeyed the Father and calls His disciples to hear and keep His words. Christian obedience flows from union with Christ, dependence on grace, and love for the Savior.

studySections.heading: Hearing Must Lead to Doing
studySections.content: James warns against hearing the Word without doing it. True reception of Scripture produces a life that responds to God.

studySections.heading: Obedience Is Not Self-Salvation
studySections.content: Believers are saved by grace through faith, not by works. Yet saving faith is never indifferent to God's commands. Obedience is fruit, not the root, of salvation.

studySections.heading: Obedience and Love for Christ
studySections.content: Jesus connects love for Him with keeping His commandments. Obedience is not cold religion when it flows from love, trust, and gratitude.

studySections.heading: Obedience in Daily Life
studySections.content: The Word shapes speech, relationships, repentance, service, suffering, forgiveness, worship, and mission. Faithfulness is practiced in ordinary steps.

sources: Scripture references listed in this doctrine entry.
